channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Nunes Marques tem a chance de se livrar da pecha de toga-gorjeta
item.description: Nunes Marques has two unique opportunities to shed the 'tip-gown' stigma, stemming from the TSE rotation and the Supreme Court's algorithms. Since such chances rarely come twice, he must act now to restore his judicial credibility.

item.title: "É muita ignorância", diz Janja sobre vídeos de pessoas bebendo detergente contaminado
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva reacted with indignation to videos showing supporters of former President Jair Bolsonaro ingesting contaminated detergent, calling the behavior 'extreme ignorance'. The videos, widely shared on social media, were condemned by health authorities and experts.

item.title: A explicação do PL para manter PP e União por perto mesmo após operação contra Ciro Nogueira
item.description: PL leadership rules out distancing itself from PP and União Brasil, key allies for Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign in pivotal states, even after the PF operation against Senator Ciro Nogueira, PP’s national president. They argue the parties are essential due to their congressional strength and state influence, stressing that one should not confuse CPF with CNPJ when assessing alliances. Flávio Bolsonaro’s inner circle believes attempts by Lula’s base to link Ciro’s name to the PL ticket are unfounded, as the senator has consistently preferred a female running mate, with Tereza Cristina being his ideal choice — despite her repeated rejections.

item.title: Lula diz que pediu a Trump a entrega de criminosos brasileiros que moram em Miami
item.description: President Lula said he asked Trump to extradite Brazilian criminals living in Miami, naming Ricardo Magro and Alexandre Ramagem as examples. He made the remark during the launch of the Brazil Against Organized Crime plan. The PT government attributed Ramage’s brief U.S. arrest to his STF conviction and PF cooperation, while the U.S. released him and expelled Brazil’s PF liaison in Florida, prompting diplomatic retaliation.

item.title: Os marqueteiros de 2026 já estão em campo
item.description: The 2026 presidential campaigns have already defined their marketing teams. Lula will continue with Raul Rabelo as his marketer, under the supervision of Sidônio Palmeira. Flávio Bolsonaro assembled a 'superteam' led by Marcello Lopes, while Romeu Zema also established his national strategy.

item.title: STF vai decidir sobre mudanças na Lei da Ficha Limpa que podem favorecer Cunha e Garotinho nas eleições deste ano
item.description: The STF will resume judgment on Supplementary Law 219/2025, which amends the Clean Record Law and could allow convicted politicians such as Eduardo Cunha, Anthony Garotinho, and José Roberto Arruda to run in the 2026 elections. The rapporteur is Minister Cármen Lúcia, and the action, filed by Rede Sustentabilidade, claims the law undermines electoral morality by shortening ineligibility periods and allowing eligibility recovery before sentence completion. The PGR advocates for a partial suspension, arguing that the ineligibility period should not run while political rights are suspended due to criminal conviction.

item.title: Trackings mostrando ‘ligeira recuperação’ de Lula aliviam PT
item.description: Internal bank trackings show a slight recovery in Lula's voting intentions following his meeting with Donald Trump, easing pressure on the PT. Though the improvement is modest, anticipation is high for tomorrow's Quaest poll release. The party views the trend as a sign of stabilization amid a challenging political landscape.

item.title: PL ainda quer Ciro Nogueira no palanque de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto said the party still wants Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) on Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential campaign slate, despite Ciro being targeted in Operation Compliance Zero over alleged financial fraud linked to Banco Master. Valdemar stated support continues unless wrongdoing is proven, stressing the right to defense. Ciro claimed the investigations are politically motivated due to the election year.

item.title: Motta diz confiar que STF dará aplicabilidade à Lei da Dosimetria
item.description: Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies, stated he will defend before the STF the applicability of the 'Dosimetry Law,' which reduces sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, emphasizing that Congress approved the bill and overturned the presidential veto by a large majority. He expressed confidence that the STF will uphold the legislative decision, despite a suspension ordered by Minister Alexandre de Moraes due to lawsuits challenging the law's constitutionality.

item.title: Pastora que denunciou violência sexual e uniu até Janja e Michelle: 'Não penso o tempo todo se é de direita ou esquerda'
item.description: Pastor Helena Raquel gained national attention after denouncing sexual and domestic violence within evangelical churches, citing Judges 19, and urged victims to report abuse rather than rely solely on prayer. Her message united supporters across political lines, including First Lady Janja da Silva and former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro. However, she faced criticism for maintaining social media ties to former President Jair Bolsonaro and his son Flávio, amid a highly polarized 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Lula diz que criará o Ministério da Segurança após Senado aprovar PEC
item.description: President Lula announced that the government will create the Ministry of Public Security once the Senate approves PEC 18/25, which has already been passed by the Chamber of Deputies. He emphasized that the proposal aims to reactivate federal involvement in public security through coordination with states and municipalities, without replacing them, and to strengthen the fight against organized crime by institutionalizing the Unified Public Security System. The PEC seeks to standardize protocols, integrate data, and streamline actions across federal entities.

item.title: Vai ter greve no metrô de SP? Funcionários decidem nesta terça
item.description: The São Paulo Metro Workers' Union will hold an assembly on Tuesday (May 12) to decide whether to strike, with potential action starting at midnight on Wednesday (May 13) if approved. The affected lines would be 1-Blue, 2-Green, 3-Red, and 15-Silver, all operated by the state government. Workers are demanding public hiring competitions, improved working conditions, health plan reforms, equal pay for equal work, and negotiations on profit-sharing (PR), citing a decade without new hires.

item.title: Motta diz que a Câmara defenderá a aplicação da Dosimetria no STF
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta stated he will defend the application of the Dosimetry Law by the STF, which reduces penalties for coup d'état and abolition of the rule of law, benefiting Bolsonaro and 849 individuals convicted for the January 8 acts. He emphasized that Congress approved the measure by a broad majority following dialogue with the Judiciary, and expressed confidence that the STF will uphold the law despite the temporary suspension by Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Damares quer barrar reeleição de deputados envolvidos com o Master
item.description: Senator Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF) announced she will directly intervene in the 2026 elections to prevent the re-election of district deputies allegedly involved in irregularities linking the Bank of Brasília (BRB) to Banco Master. Speaking during a session of the Economic Affairs Committee (CAE), she said she will lead an active campaign against these lawmakers, claiming they are tied to a network of alleged financial wrongdoing. The move aims to block the re-election of candidates accused of participating in the scheme.

item.title: Oposição cogita obstruir trabalhos da Câmara por PEC da Anistia
item.description: Opposition members to Lula's government are advocating that the PL caucus, with support from allies in Republicanos, União Brasil, and PP, obstruct Chamber of Deputies proceedings to pressure President Hugo Motta to schedule a vote on the Amnesty PEC. The proposal seeks to pardon those involved in the January 8th attacks.

item.title: Por que Nunes Marques convidou Bolsonaro e Collor, ambos presos, para a sua posse no TSE
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, the upcoming president of the TSE, invited Jair Bolsonaro and Fernando Collor, both under house arrest due to STF convictions, to his inauguration ceremony. The invitation follows protocol, extending to all living former presidents and the current officeholder, among approximately 1,500 guests. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year-and-three-month sentence for orchestrating a coup attempt after the 2022 election, while Collor was sentenced to eight years and ten months for corruption.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro escala líder do PL para evento em NY com Zema
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro appointed PL Senate leader Carlos Portinho (RJ) to represent him at an event in the United States alongside Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema (Novo). The exclusive subscriber-only article highlights a political alliance between right-wing allies in an international context.

item.title: O que tem no plano de segurança que Lula lançou a menos de cinco meses da eleição
item.description: President Lula's government launched the 'Brazil Against Organized Crime' program, allocating R$ 11 billion to combat criminal factions. The plan includes financial strangulation of crime, expansion of maximum-security prison standards, and improved homicide clearance rates, emphasizing federal-state cooperation. Announced less than five months before the presidential election, it responds to public concern, as security is the top issue for Brazilian voters.

item.title: Facções não serão donas de nenhum pedaço do Brasil, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula launched the Brazil Against Organized Crime Program, stating that criminal factions will no longer control any Brazilian territory. The program, backed by R$ 11.1 billion in initial funding and an additional R$ 10 billion via BNDES for participating states and municipalities, targets maximum-security prisons, financial strangling of crime, homicide investigations, and arms trafficking, contingent on the approval of the Public Security PEC stalled in the Senate since March.

item.title: BlackRock cravou Lula em 2026? Bruno Corano reage à projeção | BM&C NEWS
item.description: The BM&C NEWS report discusses a projection by BlackRock regarding the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, suggesting the financial institution has 'predicted' Lula as the winner. Analyst Bruno Corano reacts to the claim, questioning the validity of foreign institutions' projections in local political contexts and emphasizing the unpredictability of the Brazilian electorate. Despite technical playback issues, the video sparks debate on the influence of major asset managers in shaping electoral narratives.

item.title: Leia a íntegra do Programa Brasil Contra o Crime Organizado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) launched the Brazil Against Organized Crime Program on May 12, 2026, with a total investment of R$11 billion: R$1 billion from the Federal Budget and R$10 billion from BNDES for the states. Developed in coordination with state governments, experts, and public security forces, the initiative focuses on the prison axis to combat organized crime.

item.title: Lula e Amorim cogitam Brasil como intermediário de acordo nuclear com o Irã
item.description: President Lula and his international affairs advisor Celso Amorim have revived the proposal for Brazil to act as an intermediary in a potential nuclear agreement with Iran, amid the failure of U.S.-Iran negotiations and renewed U.S. threats of bombing resumption.

item.title: Coreia do Sul cancela vistoria e frustra governo Lula na abertura de mercado para carne brasileira
item.description: South Korea canceled planned visits to Brazilian meatpacking plants, blocking the opening of its market to Brazilian beef. This frustrates the Lula administration’s strategy to offset expected losses from new Chinese import quotas imposed at the end of 2023. The delay hinders one of Brazil’s key efforts to diversify its beef exports and reduce reliance on the Chinese market.

item.title: Lula ganha uma posição e é o 6º presidente mais popular da América Latina; veja o ranking
item.description: Lula (PT) rose from seventh to sixth place in the ranking of most popular Latin American presidents, with 49.5% positive image in May 2026, according to CB Consultora Opinión Pública. Claudia Sheinbaum of Mexico leads with 67.8%, followed by Nayib Bukele of El Salvador and other center-left and center-right leaders.

item.title: Nunes Marques assume a presidência do TSE; veja perfis dos ministros da corte
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE in 2026, with André Mendonça as vice-president, marking the first time two ministers appointed by Jair Bolsonaro to the STF simultaneously lead the electoral court. The tribunal will face challenges including the implementation of changes to the Clean Record Law and oversight of AI-generated content, while continuing its role in organizing and supervising elections, reviewing party and candidate financial reports, and adjudicating electoral disputes.

item.title: Lula diz que pediu a Trump entrega de criminosos do Brasil que estão em Miami
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated he requested Donald Trump, during a meeting at the White House, to extradite Brazilian criminals residing in Miami. The remark was made during the launch of the Brazil Against Organized Crime program, which allocates R$ 11 billion to public security.

item.title: Lula lança plano Brasil Contra o Crime Organizado, nova aposta do governo para o combate à violência
item.description: President Lula launched the 'Brazil Against Organized Crime' program, allocating up to R$ 11 billion to combat organized crime through financial asphyxiation of criminal groups, prison security strengthening, improved investigations, and arms trafficking prevention. Funded by a mix of budgetary resources and BNDES loans from the FIIS, the initiative aims to fill the void left by stalled legislative efforts in Congress. The government positions this plan as a central electoral commitment to improve Brazil’s poor public safety perception.

item.title: Plano contra crime prevê "padrão de segurança máxima" em 138 presídios
item.description: The Brazil Against Organized Crime Program, launched by President Lula, proposes implementing a "maximum security standard" in 138 state prisons, with R$ 330.6 million allocated for drones, X-ray machines, vehicles, and signal jammers. The goal is to isolate criminal leaders and prevent clandestine communication within prisons, replicating the Federal Penitentiary System model. Selected units were chosen via technical criteria and distributed across all 27 Brazilian states.

item.title: Pesquisas sobre mulheres como vice ligam alerta na campanha de Flávio
item.description: Internal polls commissioned by Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign show that selecting a woman as running mate would have limited electoral impact, with minimal gains for both male and female candidates tested. Romeu Zema (Novo), the former governor of Minas Gerais, added only one percentage point to voter intentions. Despite the weak effect, the campaign still prefers a woman on the ticket to help reduce female electorate resistance to Bolsonarism, delaying the decision until July.

item.title: Boulos diz que bets financiam críticas a Lula nas redes sociais
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (Psol) claimed that online betting companies fund social media profiles to criticize President Lula’s government, stating that some of these firms are under police investigation for irregularities. He advocated for banning online betting in Brazil, arguing it consumes workers’ free time and drives family debt, and noted that the Desenrola Brasil 2 debt renegotiation program prohibits betting for one year for participants.

item.title: Lei cria o Dia Nacional em Memória das Vítimas de Covid-19
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.406/26, establishing the National Day in Memory of Covid-19 Victims, to be observed on March 12. The date honors Rosana Aparecida Urbano, Brazil’s first fatal Covid-19 victim, whose death was followed by the loss of five family members within 50 days. The law, originating from Bill 2120/22 by Deputy Pedro Uczai (PT-SC), aims to acknowledge the pandemic’s profound social and emotional toll.

item.title: Ouvidoria em Foco: ampliação da segurança na consulta ao local de votação
item.description: The Women's Ombudsman of the TSE attended to a request from a woman in a domestic violence situation, whose ex-partner accessed her voting location through the Electoral Justice system. The ombudsman provided support, referred the victim to specialized institutions, and coordinated with the Electoral General Corregidor's Office to evaluate protective measures, including blocking voting location inquiries via the Electoral Self-Service, aiming to prevent similar risks for other women.

item.title: Rodrigo Pacheco, o Hamlet de Minas Gerais
item.description: Rodrigo Pacheco, senator from Minas Gerais and former Senate president, was overlooked by Lula for a STF seat, which went to Jorge Messias, and is now being urged to run for governor of Minas Gerais — a move that could remove him from the electoral race and weaken the PT’s 2026 strategy. His hesitation reflects a Shakespearean dilemma of loyalty, ambition, and possible resentment, with his decisions directly affecting Lula’s political positioning in the upcoming election.

item.title: 1º ministro do STF indicado por Bolsonaro, Nunes Marques assume presidência do TSE; relembre
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on November 12, succeeding Alexandre de Moraes to oversee the 2026 presidential elections. Appointed by Jair Bolsonaro in 2020, he has distanced himself from the former president after Bolsonaro’s conviction and has grown closer to Lula, maintaining an independent profile on the bench. The inauguration takes place in Brasília, with André Mendonça as vice-president, following the seniority rule among STF justices serving on the TSE.

item.title: Boulos diz que governo não aceitará fim da 6 X 1 com transição longa
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos stated that the federal government rejects proposals to end the 6×1 work schedule with a long transition period, criticizing business lobbying seeking to delay implementation by up to 10 years. He highlighted the inconsistency between the swift approval of privileges for congressmen and judiciary members and the slow pace for labor rights, warning the PEC could stall in the Senate even after House approval. The government advocates for immediate abolition of the 6×1 schedule, without salary reduction and with a 40-hour weekly workweek, impacting approximately 37 million workers.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: A reação do Congresso aos abusos de Moraes
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discussed the alleged abuses by Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF and Congress's reaction to the annulment of the Dosimetria Bill's validity. It also covered the federal government's new program to combat organized crime.

item.title: Zema volta a atacar o ex-aliado Ciro Nogueira por envolvimento no escândalo do Master
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema released a satirical video on social media implicating Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) in the Banco Master scandal, depicting him with a feminine voice accepting up to 6 million reais in bribes from bank owner Daniel Vorcaro. Although labeled as fiction and AI-generated, the video echoes Zema’s prior accusation that Nogueira is a 'sold-out politician,' despite the PP party having supported Zema’s administration and now backing his successor, Matheus Simões, for re-election in 2026.

item.title: A última esperança de Bolsonaro no STF para derrubar a condenação pela trama golpista
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's defense is attempting to use criminal revision at the STF to overturn his 27-year sentence for the coup plot, claiming incompetence of the First Chamber and denial of defense. Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, appointed by Bolsonaro, is the rapporteur, with the case to be analyzed by the Second Chamber. According to constitutional law professor Pedro Serrano, criminal revision does not apply here, as there are no exceptional circumstances to justify it, and the STF is likely to reject the request due to lack of legal foundation.

item.title: Motta defende aplicação da Lei da Dosimetria e crê em decisão favorável do STF
item.description: Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies, stated that Congress will oppose the suspension of the Dosimetry Law, approved in 2025, which allows sentence reductions for those involved in the January 8 attacks, including Jair Bolsonaro. He advocates for the STF to uphold the law’s applicability, already approved by a large congressional majority and with the presidential veto overturned. Motta expects the STF plenary to rule in favor of the law.

item.title: Movimentos articulam nome de promotora negra para o STF em encontro com Boulos
item.description: Social movements such as Instituto Juristas Negras and Mulheres Negras Decidem held a closed meeting with the Minister of the General Secretariat of the Presidency, Guilherme Boulos, to advocate for the nomination of a Black female prosecutor to the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The goal is to increase Black and female representation on Brazil’s highest court amid growing pressure for judicial diversity. The initiative reflects political and social mobilizations surrounding the upcoming STF vacancy.

item.title: As duas pesquisas de intenção de voto para presidente nesta semana
item.description: Two presidential voting intention polls will be released this week: Quaest on Wednesday (13) and Datafolha on Friday (15). Both show a tight race between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with Lula leading in the first round and a technical tie in the second round based on previous surveys. Each poll will include 2,004 interviews with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Governo deve lançar hoje plano de combate ao crime organizado
item.description: The federal government will launch today a plan to combat organized crime with an estimated investment of R$ 11 billion, focusing on financial strangulation, prison reinforcement, increased homicide clearance rates, and confrontation with arms trafficking. Implementation depends on voluntary adherence by state governments, which will gain access to funds if they adopt the proposals. The event will take place at the Palácio do Planalto with President Lula in attendance.

item.title: Petrobras vende gasolina mais barata e preocupa mercado após balanço do 1° tri
item.description: Petrobras sold gasoline below import parity price in Q1 2026, with a discount ranging from R$0.60 to R$1.20, leading to a 7.2% drop in adjusted net profit to R$32.6 billion. Analysts suggest the pricing policy reflects political interference to curb inflation and shield President Lula’s popularity, despite market dissatisfaction over reduced dividends.

item.title: Governo demorou a adotar plano de combate ao crime organizado por boicote de governadores da oposição, acusam governistas
item.description: Government allies accuse opposition governors of boycotting the Public Security PEC and the Anti-Faction Bill, delaying measures against organized crime. They claim the Lula administration could have implemented integrated federal-state actions since last year, but the articulation of governors from São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Goiás, and Santa Catarina in Congress blocked progress. While acknowledging internal divisions in Lula’s team, allies place primary blame on the opposition, particularly Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, for allegedly aligning with opponents to weaken Lula politically ahead of the 2026 presidential campaign.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 12 de maio
item.description: The decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to suspend the effects of the Dosimetry Law has triggered a new escalation in the political crisis between the opposition and the Judiciary, reigniting right-wing movements to launch an offensive against the Court. Columnist JCaesar also notes Ciro Gomes' pre-candidacy for the government of Ceará and an explosion in São Paulo's west zone that left one dead and three injured as key highlights in the VEJA roundup.

item.title: Lula sanciona, com vetos, punição mais severa a quem mata policiais
item.description: President Lula signed into law, with vetoes, a bill establishing a stricter disciplinary regime for those who kill police or military personnel on duty. He vetoed sections 3 and 4 for turning an exceptional regime into a rule and ignoring individualized sentencing, and also vetoed the ban on regime progression and conditional release for pre-trial and convicted detainees, citing unconstitutionality and conflict with public interest.

item.title: Aliados de Motta veem poucas chances para PEC da anistia antes da eleição
item.description: Allies of House Speaker Hugo Motta say the opposition’s effort to pass an Amnesty PEC before the 2026 elections has little chance of success, due to lack of political support and isolation of the initiative. Expectations are that the STF will uphold the Dosimetry Law, further weakening the opposition’s push. Even after the elections, the PEC would struggle to secure the 308 votes needed in the Chamber and 49 in the Senate.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Datafolha divulga pesquisa de intenção de voto à Presidência nesta sexta-feira
item.description: Datafolha releases a presidential voting intention poll this Friday, conducted from May 12 to 14 with 2,004 respondents. The survey, registered with TSE under BR-00290/2026, updates April data showing Lula leading with 39%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 35%, Ronaldo Caiado at 5%, and other candidates with lower support.

item.title: Operação da PF mobiliza nova Força Integrada contra o crime organizado e cumpre mais de 230 mandados em 16 estados
item.description: The Federal Police mobilizes the Integrated Force to Combat Organized Crime (FICCO) across 16 states, executing over 230 warrants for arrests and searches in operations targeting drug and arms trafficking, money laundering, and criminal factions. The action is part of the federal government’s new 'Brazil against Organized Crime' program, with R$11 billion in investments announced by President Lula. Notable operations include Paper Stone and Rota Andina in Minas Gerais, Cerco Integrado in Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina, and actions in Paraíba and Paraná.

item.title: Lula improvisa plano de segurança de R$ 11 bilhões para reeleição
item.description: Lula announced an R$11 billion plan to combat organized crime, 20 weeks before the elections, but without agreements with governors or Congress, revealing an improvised move to place public safety on the electoral agenda. The plan marks a shift in his stance, acknowledging federal responsibility for the security crisis after years of blaming state governments. Despite the investment, Lula’s rejection remains high, near 50%, according to recent polls.
